d.request: For each distinct ordersmark in orderexecutions (including null ordersmark as a separate group), count execution records, calculate the share as count/total_executions, compute difference as share minus 1/count_of_distinct_groups, return exactly 10 rows ranked by difference descending (dropping ties at rank 10 arbitrarily), with null ordersmark values last, displaying ordersmark, execution count, share, and difference without rounding.
d.sql: WITH group_counts AS (SELECT ordersmark, COUNT(*) as exec_count FROM orderexecutions GROUP BY ordersmark), totals AS (SELECT SUM(exec_count) as total_execs, COUNT(*) as num_groups FROM group_counts), with_calculations AS (SELECT gc.ordersmark, gc.exec_count, CAST(gc.exec_count AS DECIMAL(20,10)) / CAST(t.total_execs AS DECIMAL(20,10)) as share, CAST(gc.exec_count AS DECIMAL(20,10)) / CAST(t.total_execs AS DECIMAL(20,10)) - CAST(1.0 AS DECIMAL(20,10)) / CAST(t.num_groups AS DECIMAL(20,10)) as difference, CASE WHEN gc.ordersmark IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END as is_null FROM group_counts gc CROSS JOIN totals t) SELECT ordersmark, exec_count, share, difference FROM with_calculations ORDER BY is_null ASC, difference DESC LIMIT 10

c.request: For each order reference (`orderexecutions.ordersmark`, with executions lacking a reference counted together as one group), count its execution records and compute its share of all execution records. What are the top 10 order references by how far their share is above the average share across order references? Show the order reference, execution count, share and share minus the average share, without rounding, from largest difference to smallest (missing values last). Return exactly 10 rows; any rows tied with the 10th are dropped arbitrarily.
c.sql:
WITH execution_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    ordersmark,
    COUNT(*) as execution_count
  FROM orderexecutions
  GROUP BY ordersmark
),
total_executions AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) as total_exec_count
  FROM orderexecutions
),
execution_shares AS (
  SELECT 
    ec.ordersmark,
    ec.execution_count,
    ec.execution_count * 1.0 / te.total_exec_count as share
  FROM execution_counts ec
  CROSS JOIN total_executions te
),
average_share AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) as avg_share
  FROM execution_shares
),
with_differences AS (
  SELECT 
    es.ordersmark,
    es.execution_count,
    es.share,
    es.share - a.avg_share as share_diff
  FROM execution_shares es
  CROSS JOIN average_share a
)
SELECT 
  ordersmark,
  execution_count,
  share,
  share_diff
FROM with_differences
ORDER BY share_diff DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10

a.request: For each order reference (`orderexecutions.ordersmark`, with executions lacking a reference counted together as one group), count its execution records and compute its share: that count divided by the total number of execution records. Then compute the average share across order references. List the order reference, execution count, share, and share minus the average share, without rounding, sorted by that difference from largest to smallest (missing values last). Return exactly the first 10 rows; if rows tie at the 10th place, include only as many of them as needed to reach 10, chosen arbitrarily.
a.sql: WITH exec_counts AS (SELECT ordersmark, COUNT(*) as exec_count FROM orderexecutions GROUP BY ordersmark), total_count AS (SELECT SUM(exec_count) as total_execs FROM exec_counts), with_shares AS (SELECT ec.ordersmark, ec.exec_count, ec.exec_count::NUMERIC / tc.total_execs::NUMERIC as share, AVG(ec.exec_count::NUMERIC / tc.total_execs::NUMERIC) OVER () as avg_share FROM exec_counts ec CROSS JOIN total_count tc), with_diff AS (SELECT ordersmark, exec_count, share, (share - avg_share) as diff FROM with_shares) SELECT ordersmark, exec_count, share, diff FROM with_diff ORDER BY ordersmark IS NULL, diff DESC LIMIT 10;

b.request: For each unique value in `orderexecutions.ordersmark` (treating NULL as a distinct group), count execution records, calculate each group's proportion of total executions and its deviation from the average proportion, rank by deviation descending, return exactly 10 rows with the highest deviations excluding rows tied with the 10th-ranked value, sort descending by deviation with NULL references last, and display order reference, execution count, proportion, and deviation without rounding.
b.sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT COUNT(*) as total_count, COUNT(DISTINCT ordersmark) as unique_count FROM orderexecutions), execution_stats AS (SELECT ordersmark, COUNT(*) as execution_count, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / totals.total_count as proportion, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / totals.total_count - 1.0 / totals.unique_count as deviation FROM orderexecutions, totals GROUP BY ordersmark, totals.total_count, totals.unique_count), ranked AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY deviation DESC, CASE WHEN ordersmark IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as rn FROM execution_stats) SELECT ordersmark, execution_count, proportion, deviation FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 10 ORDER BY deviation DESC, CASE WHEN ordersmark IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
b.raw: For each unique value in `orderexecutions.ordersmark` (treating NULL as a distinct group), count execution records, calculate each group's proportion of total executions and its deviation from the average proportion, rank by deviation descending, return exactly 10 rows with the highest deviations excluding rows tied with the 10th-ranked value, sort descending by deviation with NULL references last, and display order reference, execution count, proportion, and deviation without rounding.
